statement: Let A = [a_0, a_1, ..., a_{sz-1}] be the sequence of values of the nodes of head in order from the head to Nil, and let j = sz - n. Then remove_nth_from_end head n returns a result r (it does not fail) such that values(r) is the sequence obtained from A by deleting the single entry a_j at 0-based index j. Equivalently, len(r) = sz - 1 and, for every i with 0 <= i < sz - 1, r[i] = a_i when i < j and r[i] = a_{i+1} when i >= j. If sz = 1 then the result is Nil (the empty sequence).
preconditions: Let sz = len(head). 1 <= sz <= 30; every value occurring in head is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 100; and 1 <= n <= sz.

statement: For every head and n satisfying the preconditions, remove_nth_from_end head n returns some result r; evaluation does not fail by arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: Let sz = len(head). 1 <= sz <= 30; every value occurring in head is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 100; and 1 <= n <= sz.

statement: Let sz = len(head). For every head and n satisfying the preconditions, whenever remove_nth_from_end head n returns a result r, the number of nodes in r is len(r) = sz - 1.
preconditions: Let sz = len(head). 1 <= sz <= 30; every value occurring in head is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 100; and 1 <= n <= sz.

statement: Let sz = len(head). For every head and n satisfying the preconditions, whenever remove_nth_from_end head n returns a result r, r = Nil if and only if sz = 1. In that case n = 1 and the single node has been removed.
preconditions: Let sz = len(head). 1 <= sz <= 30; every value occurring in head is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 100; and 1 <= n <= sz.

statement: Let A = [a_0, ..., a_{sz-1}] be the sequence of values of the nodes of head, and let r be the result returned by remove_nth_from_end head n (it does not fail). Then len(r) = sz - 1 and, for every i with 0 <= i < sz - 1, r[i] = a_i; thus exactly the final node is removed. In the case sz = 1 the result is r = Nil (the empty list).
preconditions: Let sz = len(head). 1 <= sz <= 30; every value occurring in head is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 100; and n = 1.

statement: Let A = [a_0, ..., a_{sz-1}] be the sequence of values of the nodes of head. Whenever remove_nth_from_end head n returns a result r, len(r) = sz - 1 and, for every i with 0 <= i < sz - 1, r[i] = a_{i+1}; in particular r = Nil when sz = 1. Thus exactly the original first node is removed and the remaining list is returned in the same order.
preconditions: Let sz = len(head). 1 <= sz <= 30; every value occurring in head is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 100; and n = sz.

statement: Let sz = len(head), let A = [a_0, ..., a_{sz-1}] be the sequence of values of the nodes of head, and let j = sz - n. Whenever remove_nth_from_end head n returns a result r, for every index i with 0 <= i < j, r[i] = a_i. (If j = 0 this condition is vacuous.)
preconditions: Let sz = len(head). 1 <= sz <= 30; every value occurring in head is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 100; and 1 <= n <= sz.

statement: Let sz = len(head), let A = [a_0, ..., a_{sz-1}] be the sequence of values of the nodes of head, and let j = sz - n. Whenever remove_nth_from_end head n returns a result r, for every index i with j <= i < sz - 1, r[i] = a_{i+1}. (If j = sz - 1 this condition is vacuous.)
preconditions: Let sz = len(head). 1 <= sz <= 30; every value occurring in head is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 100; and 1 <= n <= sz.

statement: Let sz = len(head), let A = [a_0, ..., a_{sz-1}] be the sequence of values of the nodes of head, let j = sz - n, and let r be any result returned by remove_nth_from_end head n. For every integer v, let count(v, L) be the number of indices i with L[i] = v. Then count(v, r) = count(v, A) - 1 if v = a_j, and count(v, r) = count(v, A) otherwise.
preconditions: Let sz = len(head). 1 <= sz <= 30; every value occurring in head is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 100; and 1 <= n <= sz.

statement: Let sz = len(head), let A = [a_0, ..., a_{sz-1}] be the sequence of values of the nodes of head, and let r be any result returned by remove_nth_from_end head n. There is an increasing sequence of indices (p_i) for 0 <= i < len(r) with 0 <= p_i < sz such that r[i] = A[p_i] for every i. Thus values(r) is a subsequence of A, preserving the original relative order.
preconditions: Let sz = len(head). 1 <= sz <= 30; every value occurring in head is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 100; and 1 <= n <= sz.

statement: Let sz = len(head), let A = [a_0, ..., a_{sz-1}] be the sequence of values of the nodes of head, and let j = sz - n. Whenever remove_nth_from_end head n returns a result r, inserting the value a_j into values(r) immediately before position j (where position j = len(values(r)) means appending at the end) produces exactly A. Equivalently, values(r) is A with the single occurrence at index j deleted.
preconditions: Let sz = len(head). 1 <= sz <= 30; every value occurring in head is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 100; and 1 <= n <= sz.

statement: Evaluating remove_nth_from_end head n leaves the argument unchanged: after the call, head still denotes the original sequence A of length sz. The returned list is a fresh List and no input node value is mutated.
preconditions: Let sz = len(head). 1 <= sz <= 30; every value occurring in head is an integer v with 0 <= v <= 100; and 1 <= n <= sz.
